CHAPTER II
ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF THE PROPOSED ACTION
A. Physical Environment
Air Quality: The quality of air in the Randolph Urban Renewal Area is one environmental consideration that is based on the amount and types of redevelopment proposed for the area. The evaluation of air quality presented herein defines applicable factors based upon preliminary analysis.
One of the main indices that the Virginia State Air Pollution Control Board uses to determine the quality of air in a given area is the recorded amount of Suspended Particulate matter. The Richmond measurement station located nearest to the project area is the Floyd Avenue Station. For the second quarter of 1972, it was found that the general area had undergone a range of measurement levels from 76-113 ug/m³, for a quarterly geometric mean of 88 ug/m³. This compares unfavorably with the National Ambient Air Quality Standard which calls for an annual geometric mean of 75 ug/m³ for Suspended Particulate matter. It should be noted, however, that this is not a condition confined to this section of the city; 7 out of a total of 11 measurement stations reported geometric means above the given Suspended Particulate standard.
A number of factors pertinent to the impact of development on air quality appear obvious. These include pollutants generated by industrial, residential, and commercial land uses; vehicular travel; and pollutants carried into the area by the prevailing meteorological conditions. Each of these pollution sources contributes to the existing air quality within the area, but pollution levels from vehicular travel would appear likely to change significantly in the future. The percentage distribution between existing and future general land use types does not appreciably change. Thus, the effect upon air quality caused by these land uses within the renewal area should not significantly change from the existing level. Moreover, this existing level could be fairly low inasmuch as the private burning of trash is prohibited within the City of Richmond.
(For the discussion of the impact of the Downtown Expressway, see Chapter II, Section A, Item 8.)
